questions.question: Which law connects addition and multiplication in a ring?
questions.explanation: Distributivity connects addition and multiplication in a ring.

questions.polish_notes: Quality round 9: rebalanced correct-answer positions to remove option-index guessing cue
questions.skill_detail: Identify the linking law in a ring.
option_explanations: The triangle inequality $\|u+v\|\le\|u\|+\|v\|$ bounds a norm under vector addition, but a ring carries no norm; the law linking its two operations is $a\cdot(b+c)=a\cdot b+a\cdot c$ and $(a+b)\cdot c=a\cdot c+b\cdot c$.

Symmetry is the entry condition $a_{ij}=a_{ji}$, equivalently $A=A^T$, a property of one square matrix under transposition, whereas the ring law links the two binary operations through $a\cdot(b+c)=a\cdot b+a\cdot c$.

Cauchy-Schwarz states $|\langle u,v\rangle|^2\le\langle u,u\rangle\langle v,v\rangle$ for an inner product, a structure a ring need not carry; the ring's connecting law is instead distributivity $a\cdot(b+c)=a\cdot b+a\cdot c$.
questions.rewrite_notes: Hand-authored explanation + per-option explanations (why each wrong option is wrong + the likely misread).
